subject: biology

moments.title: Mystery of scrapie
moments.body: Alper shows scrapie (a sheep disease) is resistant to radiation that destroys nucleic acids. The agent might be protein only. Few believe her.
moments.takeaway: A disease agent might be just protein — heretical to virology.

moments.title: Prusiner names prions
moments.body: Prusiner isolates the scrapie agent — a protein with no nucleic acid. He calls it a 'prion'. He is widely attacked. 1997 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: A protein alone can be infectious.

moments.title: BSE-vCJD link
moments.body: BSE ('mad cow disease') is linked to a new variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in humans. UK exports of beef are banned. Prion disease enters public consciousness.
moments.takeaway: Prion disease causes a public-health crisis.

moments.title: Misfolded proteins in neurodegeneration
moments.body: Amyloid-beta in Alzheimer's, alpha-synuclein in Parkinson's, tau in many dementias propagate cell-to-cell prion-like. The 'prion paradigm' extends to common diseases.
moments.takeaway: Prion-like spreading may underlie major neurodegenerative diseases.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Prion diseases remain untreatable but rare. Lecanemab and donanemab (anti-amyloid antibodies) modestly slow Alzheimer's decline.
now.open_questions: Can prion-like spreading be blocked in Alzheimer's, Parkinson's?

reflection: Prusiner was attacked for proposing protein-only inheritance of disease. Now the paradigm is mainstream. Why is virology so resistant to non-nucleic-acid heredity?
